items.title: Gut Dysbiosis at the Intersection of Depression and Addiction: A Microbiota–Gut–Brain–Reward Framework and Digital Precision Behavioural Health Agenda for the United Arab Emirates

ai.headline: Gut bacteria changes may be linked to depression and addiction through shared brain-body pathways.
ai.summary: This narrative review examined whether gut dysbiosis contributes to depression and addiction through inflammation, hormones, metabolism and reward systems. It found convergent evidence linking altered gut bacteria to both conditions, especially depression and alcohol use disorder, but concluded that causality is uncertain and routine clinical use is not yet supported.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that everyday factors like diet and gut health may be connected to mental wellbeing, though the science is still developing.

ai.fact: Gut dysbiosis is described as a potentially modifiable contributor rather than an independent cause of depression or addiction.

items.title: Efficacy of Digital Health Interventions for Insomnia: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

ai.headline: Digital sleep programmes can improve insomnia symptoms, but evidence is too uncertain to replace face-to-face therapy.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 44 randomised trials with 10,521 people found digital health interventions improved insomnia severity, sleep efficiency, total sleep time and sleep quality on average. However, prediction intervals were wide and often crossed zero, and evidence certainty was very low to moderate, so benefits may not apply everywhere or be clinically meaningful.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that app-based sleep help may work for some people, but should not be seen as a proven replacement for professional treatment.
ai.life_skill: Try a reputable digital sleep programme as a first step, but speak to a qualified health professional if insomnia persists or affects daily life.
ai.fact: Digital health interventions for insomnia showed statistically significant average improvements across several sleep outcomes in pooled randomised trials.

quiz.question: What did the review conclude about using digital health interventions instead of face-to-face cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia?
quiz.answer: They cannot be recommended as a standard substitute, though they may serve as a low-intensity option in stepped care.

ai.caveat: The evidence is exploratory, with wide prediction intervals crossing zero and very low-to-moderate certainty, so average benefits may not hold in every setting.

items.title: Network meta-analysis of the efficacy of different exercise therapies in patients with knee osteoarthritis.

ai.headline: Different exercises help knee osteoarthritis in different ways: mind-body for pain and stiffness, strength training for muscle strength.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 51 randomised trials with 3,045 people who had knee osteoarthritis. Mind-body exercise reduced pain and stiffness most, mixed exercise improved knee function most, and strength training improved muscle strength most.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that choosing the right type of exercise can target specific problems like pain, stiffness, or weak muscles in knee osteoarthritis.
ai.life_skill: Try mixing gentle mind-body movement with strength exercises if you have knee pain, but check with a qualified health professional first.
ai.fact: Mind-body exercise was linked to the greatest reductions in pain and stiffness among people with knee osteoarthritis in this review.

quiz.question: Which exercise was most effective for improving muscle strength in people with knee osteoarthritis?
quiz.answer: Strength training was most effective for enhancing muscle strength.

ai.caveat: The authors say the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of uncertainty and limitations in the available evidence.

ai.headline: School nutrition policies and free meals are linked to more students eating school meals and better diets.
ai.summary: This umbrella review looked at 18 systematic reviews of school-based nutrition policies and environmental changes in the US. It found consistent links between strategies like breakfast after the bell, food environment policies, and universal free school meals and higher meal participation, with some evidence of better diet quality.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how school rules and meal programmes can shape what children eat and their chances of healthier diets.

quiz.answer: Positive associations with school meal participation.

ai.caveat: It is an umbrella review of existing systematic reviews, most of which were low quality, and few studies examined weight-related outcomes.

items.title: Occupational health outcomes among migrant and non-migrant construction workers: A systematic review and narrative synthesis

ai.headline: Migrant construction workers face higher fatal and general injury rates than non-migrant workers.
ai.summary: This systematic review compared occupational health outcomes between migrant and non-migrant construction workers across 38 studies in 15 countries. Migrant workers had higher rates of fatal and general occupational injury, including excess risk for fatal falls, traumatic brain injury, heat-related mortality, and ocular trauma, though patterns for non-fatal injuries and other health problems were mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that migrant status is linked to workplace safety risks in construction, highlighting the need for better protections and multilingual safety training.
ai.life_skill: Check that safety instructions at work are available in a language you fully understand.
ai.fact: Migrant construction workers experienced higher rates of fatal and general occupational injury than non-migrant construction workers.

quiz.question: What did the review find about fatal and general occupational injury rates between migrant and non-migrant construction workers?
quiz.answer: Migrant construction workers experienced higher rates of fatal and general occupational injury than non-migrants.

ai.caveat: Most included studies were of low to moderate quality and primarily conducted in high-income settings.
